answer.headline: O Hare is more congested than Midway on taxi-out and NAS delay
answer.body: Of the two Chicago airports in this comparison, Chicago O Hare (ORD) is more congested than Chicago Midway (MDW) on taxi-out and NAS (airspace/system) delay. Average taxi-out was {F22} minutes at ORD and {F21} minutes at MDW, a calculated gap of {F39} minutes. Median taxi-out was {F24} minutes at ORD and {F23} minutes at MDW. NAS delay per arrival was {F32} minutes at ORD and {F31} minutes at MDW, a calculated gap of {F41} minutes. Average departure delay was {F30} minutes at ORD and {F29} minutes at MDW. The arrival delay rate was {F28} at ORD and {F27} at MDW, and the cancellation rate was {F36} at ORD and {F35} at MDW. The departure delay rate is the exception: {F25} at MDW versus {F26} at ORD, and the calculated MDW minus ORD gap is {F40}. Weather delay per arrival was {F34} minutes at ORD and {F33} minutes at MDW. The catalog scheduled peak-hour metric was {F38} operations per hour at ORD and {F37} operations per hour at MDW. Those peak figures are observed schedule counts, not a congestion rate.

claims.text: Average taxi-out over the comparison window was {F22} minutes at ORD and {F21} minutes at MDW.
The calculated ORD minus MDW average taxi-out gap is {F39} minutes.
Median taxi-out was {F24} minutes at ORD and {F23} minutes at MDW.
NAS delay per arrival was {F32} minutes at ORD and {F31} minutes at MDW.
The calculated ORD minus MDW NAS-delay gap is {F41} minutes.
Average departure delay was {F30} minutes at ORD and {F29} minutes at MDW.
The arrival delay rate was {F28} at ORD and {F27} at MDW.
The cancellation rate was {F36} at ORD and {F35} at MDW.
The departure delay rate was {F25} at MDW and {F26} at ORD. The calculated MDW minus ORD gap is {F40}.
Weather delay per arrival was {F34} minutes at ORD and {F33} minutes at MDW.
The catalog scheduled peak-hour metric was {F38} operations per hour at ORD and {F37} operations per hour at MDW.

ORD is the more congested Chicago airport when congestion is read from taxi-out and NAS delay. Those gaps line up with a higher average departure delay, a higher arrival delay rate, and a higher cancellation rate at ORD. The higher departure delay rate at MDW means a larger share of MDW departures were late, which is a different statistic from how long aircraft waited or how much airspace delay they absorbed.

assumptions: Chicago is bound to the two airports in the Chicago-Naperville-Elgin, IL-IN CBSA that are in the city of Chicago: Chicago O Hare International (ORD) and Chicago Midway International (MDW). Chicago Rockford International is in Rockford, in a different CBSA, and is excluded.

More congested is judged primarily by average and median taxi-out and by NAS delay per arrival. Average departure delay, arrival delay rate, and cancellation rate are supporting operational-stress measures. The departure delay rate is reported separately because it ranks the two airports in the opposite direction.
The comparison uses the latest window those On-Time metrics fully cover, which is the window labeled on the findings.
limitations: On-Time statistics cover domestic flights of reporting carriers only. International flights and small carriers are excluded. On-Time coverage of airline departures was {F45} at ORD and {F44} at MDW. International seat share over the same window was {F43} at ORD and {F42} at MDW, so a larger share of ORD seats sits outside the domestic On-Time sample.

Weather delay per arrival is also higher at ORD ({F34} versus {F33}). The dataset does not allocate the taxi-out gap across weather, airline scheduling, and airfield or airspace capacity. NAS delay is the airspace/system component, not a causal attribution.

Scheduled peak-hour operations are a lower bound because they include reporting carriers only. Open-runway counts are {F47} at ORD and {F46} at MDW, but runway count is not capacity. Peak operations are not converted into a utilization rate.
Terminal capacity, unmet demand, fares, and profitability are not measured here. This comparison is not a valuation and not an investment screen.
